title: driver-matrix-sanity-probe-report-terraform-integration
content:
Summary:
This note captures a compact, reproducible sanity probe and field report for validating Kubernetes + GPU driver / CUDA / NCCL combinations during Terraform-driven upgrades for Redwood Private deployments (VPC/on-prem). Purpose is pragmatic: give SREs and infra engineers a short checklist, a small empirical matrix from lab runs, and actionable Terraform module notes for safe canary/rollout behavior. Not a final playbook — intended as an iterative lab-to-field artifact.

Scope and constraints:
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 40GB (PCIe) and 3090-class nodes available in lab.
- OS baseline: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS kernel 5.15 and RHEL 8.8 with 4.18 kernel variant tested in separate runs.
- Container runtime: containerd 1.6.x primary; one trial with Docker 20.10 for regression repro.
- Kubernetes control plane: 1.25 through 1.28 tested. Production target for next quarter: 1.27.
- Terraform: private-deployments modules v0.12.x (module ref githash: a1b2c3d)

Empirical sanity matrix (summary of lab runs — green = pass, amber = degraded, red = fail):
- Rows: Driver version | CUDA | NCCL | K8s | container runtime | MPS | Result | Notes
- 525.85 | 12.1 | 2.18 | 1.25 | containerd 1.6 | disabled | green | stable perf, KV cache warm OK
- 535.54 | 12.2 | 2.19 | 1.26 | containerd 1.6 | disabled | amber | occasional kernel oops on heavy concurrent small-batch tokenize (investigate scheduler)
- 470.199 | 11.7 | 2.10 | 1.25 | containerd 1.6 | enabled | red | MPS broke with containerd+MIG interplay on A100; driver reprod on Ubuntu only
- 535.86 | 12.2 | 2.19 | 1.27 | containerd 1.6 | disabled | green | best latency at small token sizes, recommended for canary
- 465.19 | 11.4 | 2.8 | 1.24 | docker 20.10 | disabled | red | NCCL collective hangs in multi-pod allreduce (old cuda stack)

Key observations (unique findings from this run):
1) containerd+MPS: MPS works functionally with containerd, but there is a race during GPU reclamation when pods are rapidly cycled. Happened only with certain driver builds; workaround: add graceful drain + sleep 15s in pre-stop hook.
2) Kernel oops pattern: observed RT_MUTEX deadlock trace when running many small concurrent inferences using the 535.54 driver on our 5.15 kernel. Appears mitigated by setting the scheduler tunable: kernel.sched_min_granularity_ns=20000000 on nodes.
3) NCCL version mismatches: images built with NCCL 2.10 show hangs when the host driver exposes a 2.18-compatible kernel interface; ensure runtime container NCCL is <= driver-reported NCCL ABI compatibility. Prefer shipping NCCL inside images only when pinned and matched to driver major version.

Minimal validation probe (runnable steps for canary node):
- Pre-checks on candidate node:
  - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version --format=csv
  - uname -r; cat /etc/os-release
  - containerd --version && crictl --version
- Deploy tiny canary workload (k8s manifest included below) that does: single-pod, single-container image with CUDA 12.2 runtime, NCCL 2.19, and a tiny synthetic benchmark that performs repeated 512-token generation loops (1s sleep between loops).
- Observe for 30 minutes: GPU utilization, nv_peer_mem logs, dmesg for oops, kubelet logs for eviction/oom-killer events.
- Smoke metrics to be collected (Prometheus labels): node_gpu_temp_c, node_gpu_power_w, container_gpu_memory_bytes, pod_inference_latency_p50/p95.

Sample k8s manifest for canary (conceptual snippet to paste):
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gpu-canary-probe
spec:
  containers:
    - name: infer
      image: redwoodci/cuda12.2-nccl2.19-probe:202507
      resources:
        limits:
          nvidia.com/gpu: 1
      lifecycle:
        preStop:
          exec:
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 15"]

Terraform module notes (practical pointers, variable-level checks):
- module "gpu_node_pool": ensure variable enable_mig default = false; add a regression gate variable enable_mps_safe_reclaim (default false) until MPS drain behavior is hardened.
- Expose a node taint variable gpu_upgrade_taint = { key = "redwood/gpu-upgrade", value = "true", effect = "NoSchedule" } so Terraform can mark nodes during upgrade windows.
- Add lifecycle create_before_destroy = false on node pool autoscaling group resources to avoid double-binding GPUs during provider transitions.
- Provide an opt-in pre-flight null_resource that runs the nvidia-smi and kernel tunables check via remote-exec. Fail fast if mismatched.

Upgrade/rollout plan (canary -> phased):
1) Preflight: run probe on staging cluster; collect 2x 30m runs spaced by 12h.
2) Canary: select 2 nodes in one AZ, cordon + drain with custom drain script that enforces preStop sleep. Deploy updated node image with new driver/cuda. Run 1h synthetic traffic with 5x concurrent canaries.
3) Phased: roll 10% node pool every 2 hours with automated health checks. Health criteria: no node-level kernel oops, average p95 latency within 10% of baseline, no OOMs, no NCCL collectives timeout.
4) Full: after 48h stable, roll remaining nodes night window.

Rollback triggers and fast rollback steps:
- Triggers: repeated kernel oops, >2% request error rate increase, repeated container restarts >3x per pod within 15m, NCCL allreduce hangs.
- Immediate rollback: Terraform apply to previous module version that pins driver image and node image id. We keep AMI/image id of last-good as variable last_known_good_image. Also recommended: re-run node drain with uncordon order reversed to reassign traffic back.

Observability and post-mortem artifacts to gather on failures:
- Full dmesg and journalctl -k for each affected node.
- nv-hostengine logs and libnvidia-container logs from the kubelet host.
- cp /var/log/nvidia-installer.log if present.
- Export contiguous core dumps and attach to issue with steps to reproduce.

Open questions and proposed experiments (for next lab cycle):
- Can kernel 6.x show the same RT_MUTEX pattern? We need a controlled run on 6.1 in parallel to validate scheduler tunables.
- MPS + containerd unexpected reclaim pattern: reproduce with pod churn 60s lifecycle to see thresholds. If confirmed, explore patch in containerd GPU plugin to serially drain MPS contexts.
- Quantify NCCL ABI surface: run cross-driver NCCL allreduce across mixed driver hosts (535.x and 525.x) to see behavior and document safe mixing rules.

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- Aisha: add terraform opt-in preflight null_resource and expose gpu_upgrade_taint var (ETA: 2025-07-25).
- Diego: reproduce kernel oops on 535.54 on 6.1 kernel and report traces (ETA: 2025-08-01).
- Evelyn: integrate canary probe job into CI (small nightly run) and add Prometheus alerts for nv-hostengine anomalies (ETA: 2025-07-30).
- Samira: draft a customer-facing note summarizing expected maintenance behavior for upcoming Private cluster upgrades (ETA: 2025-08-05).

Appendix: quick commands for SREs during an incident:
- gather: sudo journalctl -k -u kubelet --no-pager > /tmp/kubelet.journal.txt; sudo dmesg -T > /tmp/dmesg.txt; sudo nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/nvidia-smi.txt
- force-uncordon: kubectl uncordon <node> || echo failed; # to reintroduce node quickly after rollback
- pin driver: terraform apply -var 'node_image_id=ami-abcdef1234' -auto-approve

Notes on uniqueness: this doc intentionally focuses on a compact canary-oriented probe, concrete kernel tunable observation, containerd+MPS reclaim behavior and Terraform-level gating variables. It is meant to complement larger playbooks rather than supplant them.

End of note.
